Gross primary production and community respiration were tightly coupled during the spring bloom.

gross O2 evolution rates determined from fast repetition fluorometry (FRR) were tightly coupled to in situ pH-based gross inorganic carbon (C) uptake during a spring phytoplankon bloom in Esthawate Water, UK.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of FRR-based measurements to assess the photosynthetic activity of phytoplankton in the natural environment and the use of pH measurements to determine the rate of net and gross CO2 assimilation.
the development of novel in situ techniques for the measurement of gross photosynthetic electron transport and inorganic CO2 assimilation.
the development of a new method for determining gross primary production (GPP) in the field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FRR-based approach provides a reliable and robust measure of daily gross photosynthesis and that this approach is a valuable tool for the study of lake community metabolism.
gross photosynthetic O2 evolution and net and gross in situ CO2 assimilation were tightly coupled throughout the bloom and were driven by the photosynthetic activity of the bloom.
gross primary production, gross respiration, and net community production are all tightly coupled and are all controlled by the daily rate of gross photosynthetic electron transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FRR technique is an excellent tool for determining in situ rates of gross photosynthesis and that the technique is robust enough to be used for a range of applications, such as the estimation of community respiration and net community production, and for the determination of the photosynthesizing fraction of the phytoplankton community.
daily gross O(2) production was driving daily gross CO2 assimilation, and that the latter was driving daily changes to community metabolism.
gross O2 evolution measurements made using the FRR fluorometer can be used as an effective tool to determine gross CO2 uptake rates in situ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gross photosynthesis is the most important factor driving daily changes in net community metabolism.
the FRR-based approach to measuring photosynthetic electron transport is a useful tool for understanding community metabolism.
gross O2 production can be used to estimate gross CO2 uptake, thus providing a means of determining gross primary productivity (GPP) and net community production (NCP).
